title: V6 selected LinkReport lineage across both writers
finding: The historical default-graph CAS-conflict claim was incorrect: in the pre-fix actual-node pair both writers succeeded with the same deterministic LinkReport artifact ID and payload, while returning distinct manifest-selected views. The real gap was selector and lineage consistency across the complete two-writer set.
change: LinkTrinity uses input_ref_from_artifact_ref with canonical `ir` and `registry_bundle` roles and requests the selected output profile. CompileFoundry passes the existing return_selected_profile=true selector through CompileRequest. Different upstream lineage views remain distinct.

verification.focused_unit_tests: 10 passed; full output and exact command are cited in the raw source-freeze packet.
verification.actual_cas_pair_controls: Passed for profileless API-like inputs and selected Trinity/registry refs using the actual node implementations and DefaultFoundryPort.
verification.ruff: Canonical product-root Ruff check and format check passed on all six changed paths.
verification.default_worker_route: The 23-node route test collects but was not run. Its live worker, all-alias trace, simulation and fresh-read behavior remain pending independent review and one bounded route run.

p38_property_and_divergent_case.property: When both actual writers consume the same exact typed refs, they return the same exact selected LinkReport ArtifactRef and the report manifest preserves the same canonical input edges.
p38_property_and_divergent_case.old_proxy: Comparing only artifact ID and report payload.
p38_property_and_divergent_case.divergent_case: Before the repair, both real nodes succeeded with the same artifact ID and report payload, but LinkTrinity returned a profileless ref with input role trinity_bundle while CompileFoundry returned a profile-bound ref with role ir. A selected-LinkTrinity/default-CompileFoundry control also returned unequal exact refs, so both writer selectors and canonical input roles are required.
